Title: GSMC partners with Kenya Editors Guild to deliver solution-oriented discussions for media
NewsSummary: Aga Khan University Graduate School of Media and Communications has partnered with the Kenya Editors Guild to deliver solution-oriented discussions for media
NewsContent:
East Africa's media is grappling with the effect of the COVID-19 pandemic. The virus not only fast-tracked a business ailment which had been eating away at the media's advertising and audiences - diminishing revenues all around - but also forced the hurried adoption of new production processes and reshaping of news platforms which would have been unimaginable a few years ago.

Aga Khan University's Graduate School of Media and Communications (GSMC) and the Kenya Editors Guild (KEG) have partnered to deliver a series of talks that will bring together selected groups of editors and media managers and notable industry experts from Africa and beyond, for free-ranging, solution-oriented discussions.

The series dubbed, "Media Watchtower", held the first discussion on November 30, 2020, with Styli Charalambous, CEO of the South African news publisher the Daily Maverick delivering the keynote speech. He shared valuable insights into the membership revenue model, in which the company's news outlets have had globally-acclaimed success. "Sustainability is the biggest issue facing the media today. The old way of cookie-cutter revenue model is dead with many revenue opportunities requiring a bespoke strategy. New skills and knowledge are required and we made an active decision to develop the most experienced newsroom in South Africa by building the talent of the group as a whole."

In organizing the seminars, KEG and GSMC recognise that in East Africa, as elsewhere, the COVID-19 pandemic has aggravated the effects of digital disruption on traditional media. On top of shrinking revenues, news publishers have suffered upheaval in their production processes and distribution networks - giving urgency to media's search for new revenue models.

GSMC continues to invest in the improvement of the quality of media practitioners through its programs, some of which are designed specifically for the media fraternity. It is committed to keeping the knowledge discourse alive among media practitioners, and in so doing hopes to help contribute to quality training and nurturing of seasoned media practitioners.

The Kenya Editors' Guild is a professional society that brings together senior editors in print, digital, broadcast and other electronic media. It seeks to: defend and promote free and independent media in Kenya; promote quality and ethical journalism; provide a forum for the discussion of the issues facing the media and editors; and to network with other professional organisations.
